key_insight: Thermally insulating the absorber can relax the need to prevent electron-to-lattice energy transfer, while allowing some ohmic heat to be recycled into electrical work.
engineering_relevance: The analysis identifies thermal insulation, electrical conductivity, and suppression of contact heat leakage as design priorities for high-efficiency hot-carrier and hot-absorber solar cells.
method: Analyze thermally insulated absorbers with electron-to-lattice energy transfer.
Include ohmic losses from finite absorber conductivity and evaluate heat recycling.
Assess sensitivity to finite contact-mediated heat leakage.
evidence_signal: The thermodynamic analysis finds that ohmic heat can be partially recovered with an efficiency given by the Carnot factor and evaluates sensitivity to contact heat leakage.
watch_item: The cited 85.4% hot-carrier efficiency limit is not a practical device projection; high efficiencies require ideal energy-selective contacts and negligible parasitic contact conductance.
paper_title: Nonideal Absorbers in Hot-Carrier and Hot-Absorber Solar Cells: Losses and Heat Recycling
